hero.title: Body Fat Percentage Explained
hero.lead:
Body fat percentage is the share of your weight that is fat, as opposed to muscle, bone, organs, and water. Two people can weigh the same with wildly different figures — which is why this number tells you things the scale and the BMI chart cannot.

Below: the healthy ranges for men and women, how much to trust each method — less than the display suggests — and how to use the number well.

sections.heading: What body fat percentage actually measures
sections.html:
Body fat comes in two kinds; only one is optional.

Essential fat is structural: organ cushioning, insulation, hormone production. Men need roughly 2 to 5 percent; women considerably more, around 10 to 13 percent, largely for reproductive health. Dropping below is genuinely dangerous, not impressively lean.

Storage fat is the reserve — the layer under the skin plus visceral fat around the abdominal organs. Visceral fat is most strongly linked to type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and heart disease — and responds fastest when you become more active.

The percentage folds all of it into one figure: how much fat you carry, but not where — which is why it pairs so well with waist-to-height ratio, a direct read on visceral fat.

sections.heading: Healthy body fat percentage ranges
sections.html:
Unlike BMI, the ranges are sex-specific — women carry substantially more essential fat. The widely used adult categories:

Men

CategoryBody fatWhat it looks like
Essential fat2 – 5%Physiological minimum; not sustainable
Athletes6 – 13%Visible definition; typical of competition
Fitness14 – 17%Lean and athletic; maintainable year-round
Acceptable18 – 24%The healthy middle for most men
High25% and aboveCorresponds broadly to obesity; worth a doctor's input

Women

CategoryBody fatWhat it looks like
Essential fat10 – 13%Physiological minimum; not sustainable
Athletes14 – 20%Visible definition; typical of competition
Fitness21 – 24%Lean and athletic; maintainable year-round
Acceptable25 – 31%The healthy middle for most women
High32% and aboveCorresponds broadly to obesity; worth a doctor's input

Two caveats. Body fat rises with age at a stable weight, so a few points above the "fitness" band in your fifties is unremarkable. Sitting very low for long carries real costs, particularly for women — disrupted or absent periods, bone density loss, hormonal problems. Lower is not automatically better.

sections.heading: How the measurement methods compare
sections.html:
Every method estimates rather than measures, and they disagree — sometimes by a lot.

MethodHow it worksTypical errorPracticality
DEXA scanLow-dose X-ray separates fat, lean tissue, and boneAbout 1 – 2 pointsClinic or sports lab; the practical gold standard
Hydrostatic weighingWeighed while submerged in waterAbout 2 pointsResearch settings; you must exhale fully underwater
Air displacement (Bod Pod)Measures body volume in a sealed chamberAbout 2 – 3 pointsUniversity and sports facilities; quick and comfortable
Skinfold calipersPinch thickness at 3 to 7 sites into a formulaAbout 3 – 5 points, skill-dependentCheap and portable; varies a lot between testers
Tape measure (Navy method)Neck, waist, and hips into an equationAbout 3 – 5 pointsFree and repeatable at home
Smart scale (bioimpedance)Weak electrical current estimates lean massOften 4 – 8 points, sometimes moreEffortless daily use; heavily affected by hydration
Visual comparison chartMatching yourself to reference photosWide, but rarely worse than a bad scaleFree; surprisingly serviceable for tracking direction

About the bioimpedance scales most people own: current travels more easily through water, so hydration moves the reading — a workout or a salty meal can swing it several points with no change in your body. They are trend instruments, not measurement instruments.

sections.heading: Getting a number you can actually use
sections.html:
Since every home method has meaningful error, chase consistency, not accuracy — an imprecise method used identically still shows the direction.

  • One method, always. Comparing a caliper to a smart scale only proves they disagree.
  • Same conditions. Morning, after the bathroom, before eating or exercise.
  • Judge by the month. Daily movement is mostly hydration noise — the same phenomenon behind ordinary daily weight fluctuation.
  • Track it alongside weight, not instead. Weight flat while body fat falls is what recomposition looks like — invisible if you only watch the scale.

Read together with BMI and a waist measurement — the most reliable home measurement there is — the numbers rarely all mislead at once. A reading that genuinely worries you belongs with your doctor, who can order a proper assessment.

sections.heading: Tracking it: spreadsheet vs app
sections.html:
A spreadsheet handles this — date, weight, body fat. What it costs is friction, and records kept that way tend to stop at three weeks, right before the trend turns readable.

The free Weight Journal Feeltracker app is the low-friction version: it logs weight in kilograms or pounds, calculates BMI, records body fat alongside, and charts each with a trend line. It syncs with Apple Health — a smart scale that writes there can feed it — and across your devices via iCloud, no account, no email. Reminders, widgets, and PDF, XLSX, CSV, or JSON export are built in; optional AI insights summarize your history.

Wherever you record it: one method, same conditions, patience with the number.

items.question: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
items.answer: Broadly **18 to 24 percent for men** and **25 to 31 percent for women**, with the leaner "fitness" bands just below. Both ranges shift upward slightly with age, and going far below them carries its own health risks.

items.question: Are smart scales accurate for body fat?
items.answer: Not as absolute numbers. Bioimpedance scales pass a small current through your body, and hydration changes the result — errors of 4 to 8 percentage points are common. They are still useful for tracking **direction** if you measure under identical conditions every time.

items.question: Is body fat percentage better than BMI?
items.answer: It answers a better question but is much harder to measure well. [BMI](/weight/bmi-chart/) is crude and precise; body fat is meaningful and imprecise. Most people are best served by watching both, plus a waist measurement.

items.question: How fast can body fat percentage change?
items.answer: Slowly. Real composition change shows up over weeks and months — anything moving several points in a week is measurement noise, usually hydration. Expect at least a month of consistent readings before a trend means anything.

items.question: Can body fat be too low?
items.answer: Yes, and it is a genuine medical concern, not an achievement. Below the essential-fat threshold the body cannot maintain hormone production; in women this commonly shows up as disrupted or absent periods and reduced bone density. If you are training toward very low levels, do it with medical supervision.

data.disclaimerText: This article is for general information only and is not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Home body fat measurements are estimates with wide margins of error and cannot assess your health on their own — always discuss body composition, weight targets, and any plan to change them with your doctor or healthcare provider. Seek medical advice if you are losing weight without trying, if periods stop or become irregular, or if very low body fat comes with fatigue, frequent illness, or stress fractures.
